# PregnancyRights.Law

> Pregnancy discrimination lawyers for California workers and working mothers. Help with pregnancy leave, accommodations, lactation breaks, reproductive loss leave, and retaliation.

PregnancyRights.Law is operated by Centurion Trial Attorneys, APC, a California employment law firm. Attorney responsible: Ryan Stygar. Phone: 1-888-CALL-RYAN.

## Pages
- [Accessibility Statement](https://pregnancyrights.law/accessibility/): How PregnancyRights.Law works to be usable by everyone, the accessibility options on this site, and how to get help if something doesn't work for you.
- [Pregnancy Rights Guides](https://pregnancyrights.law/articles/): Plain-English guides to pregnancy, leave, accommodation, lactation, and reproductive loss rights for California workers, plus pregnancy cases in the news.
- [Danielle Rini, Litigation Counsel](https://pregnancyrights.law/danielle-rini/): Danielle Rini is Litigation Counsel at Centurion Trial Attorneys, APC, the firm behind PregnancyRights.Law and SueMyBoss.Law, fighting for California workers.
- [Pregnancy Rights FAQ](https://pregnancyrights.law/faq/): Answers to common questions about pregnancy at work in California: discrimination, leave, accommodations, pumping breaks, reproductive loss leave, and deadlines.
- [Pregnancy Discrimination Lawyers for California Workers | PregnancyRights.Law](https://pregnancyrights.law/): Pregnant, a new mom, or pushed out after a pregnancy? Know your California rights to leave, accommodations, and pumping breaks. No fee unless we win.
- [Disclaimer and Privacy](https://pregnancyrights.law/legal/): Attorney advertising disclaimer and privacy information for PregnancyRights.Law, operated by Centurion Trial Attorneys, APC.
- [Case Results](https://pregnancyrights.law/results/): Pregnancy discrimination, retaliation, and wrongful termination results our firm has obtained for California employees. Prior results do not guarantee a similar outcome.
- [Attorney Ryan Stygar](https://pregnancyrights.law/ryan-stygar/): Ryan Stygar is a California workers' rights employment attorney, former firefighter, and author of Get It in Writing (Penguin), followed by millions on social media.

## Guides
- [Former Brooklyn Nets Executive Sues, Saying He Was Fired After Taking Parental Leave](https://pregnancyrights.law/articles/brooklyn-nets-parental-leave-lawsuit/): A former Brooklyn Nets vice president alleges in a new federal lawsuit that the team fired him after he took leave to care for his newborn son.
- [California Proposes New Pregnancy Rules That Would Count Telework as an Accommodation](https://pregnancyrights.law/articles/california-proposed-pregnancy-leave-accommodation-rules/): California's Civil Rights Council proposed updated pregnancy leave and accommodation rules covering telework, postpartum depression, and bonding leave.
- [How Do I Ask for a Pregnancy Accommodation at Work in California?](https://pregnancyrights.law/articles/how-to-ask-for-pregnancy-accommodation-california/): How to ask your California employer for a pregnancy accommodation, what your doctor's note needs to say, deadlines, and a sample request.
- [Fired While Pregnant in California? What to Do in the First Week](https://pregnancyrights.law/articles/fired-while-pregnant-first-week/): Fired while pregnant in California? What to do in the first week: final pay, your records, unemployment or disability benefits, and deadlines.
- [Smithfield Agrees to Settle EEOC Pregnancy Discrimination and Wrongful Termination Suit](https://pregnancyrights.law/articles/smithfield-eeoc-pregnancy-accommodation-settlement/): Smithfield agreed to settle an EEOC lawsuit alleging it denied a pregnant worker's accommodations, forced unpaid leave, then fired her.
- [Do I Get Lactation Breaks at Work in California?](https://pregnancyrights.law/articles/lactation-breaks-california/): California law requires break time and a private, non-bathroom space to pump at work. Here is what your employer owes you and what to do if it says no.
- [What Are My Pregnancy Rights at Work in California?](https://pregnancyrights.law/articles/pregnancy-rights-at-work-california/): California pregnancy rights at work: protection from discrimination, accommodations, up to four months of disability leave, and bonding leave.
- [Do I Get Time Off After a Miscarriage in California?](https://pregnancyrights.law/articles/reproductive-loss-leave-california/): California law gives eligible workers up to five days of leave after a miscarriage, stillbirth, or other reproductive loss. Here is how it works.
